limitations: Proteomic differential expression analyses reveal observational associations between circulating protein concentrations and autoimmune disease states (RA, SLE vs Healthy controls); they do not demonstrate whether altered protein levels cause disease pathogenesis, represent downstream inflammatory responses, or reflect medication effects.

Targeted proximity extension assay (PEA) panels measure relative protein abundances for predefined protein sets and cannot quantify absolute molecular concentrations or cell counts without validated absolute standard curves.
None of the top 12 discordant proteins had blood mass spectrometry concentration records in HPA, precluding cross-platform orthogonal validation by MS.

limitations: Differential expression results represent statistical associations with disease status in blood PEA profiling and do not establish causal mechanisms, direct tissue pathology, or disease etiology.

Blood concentration entries from immunoassay (IM) and mass spectrometry (MS) in the proteinatlas master table reflect specific targeted profiling studies and detection thresholds, so the absence of a recorded value indicates missing measurement/undetected status in those specific assays rather than complete absence from blood.
PEA measurements reflect relative normalized protein levels and affinity probe binding, which may be influenced by epitope availability, complex formation, or technical sensitivity limits.
